payload.title: [blob-gc-1] Async derivative persistence is fire-and-forget: silent data loss + unhandled-rejection worker crash
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING blob-gc-1 (high/data-loss, confidence=high, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: apps/server/src/blobs/processor-job.ts
LINES: 74-94, 152-161

WHAT: In this release BlobDerivativeStore.record() was changed from synchronous (returns DerivativeRow) to async (returns Promise<DerivativeRow>) — see the diff of apps/server/src/storage/blob-derivative-store.ts (base had `record(input): DerivativeRow` at line 75). The caller persistDerivative() in processor-job.ts was NOT updated: it is still declared `: void` (line 80) and invokes `derivatives.record({...})` at line 82 WITHOUT await. The handler loop (lines 153-161) calls persistDerivative synchronously, then immediately returns `{ status: 'completed', result: { derivatives: derivatives.length } }` (lines 168-171). The DB write is therefore a floating promise that escapes the surrounding try/catch (the catch only covers the synchronous call, not the detached promise). Two concrete failures: (1) the blob.process job is marked COMPLETED before the derivative bytes are durably written, and because completed jobs never retry, a write that is still pending when the process restarts is permanently lost — the thumbnail/transcode/moderation sidecar silently never exists; (2) if record() rejects (DB constraint, disk full, Postgres connection drop), it becomes an unhandled promise rejection with no .catch and no global process.on('unhandledRejection') handler anywhere in server.ts/worker.ts/index.ts, which under modern Node terminates the worker process.

IMPACT: Derivative data (thumbnails, transcoded variants, and — via moderationProcessor — content-moderation verdict sidecars used to gate access) can be silently dropped without the job ever retrying. A single transient DB error on a derivative write can crash the entire job-worker process. Moderation-decision loss is a security-relevant side effect (access gating on a missing verdict).

SUGGESTED FIX: Make persistDerivative async (return Promise<void>) and await derivatives.record(...); then `await persistDerivative(...)` inside the handler loop (or Promise.all the batch). Any rejection then surfaces in the handler's try/catch and the job correctly reports failed+retryable instead of completed.
